newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2952 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2960 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai, unaffected by comments from Vice Premier Zhu Rongji on China's foreign exchange reserves, dealers said.
A newspaper in Taiwan reported on Tuesday that Zhu, who is in charge of China's economy, said Beijing's foreign exchange reserves were expected to reach $150 billion in 1997.
Dealers said that as his comments were not released to major mainland media, the local market had no active response and the yuan continued to consolidate.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2960.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2950 and consolidated in a narrow range of 8.2950 and 8.2960 for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2961 and a high of 8.2906.
Trading was more active than on Monday, with most trading done at the 8.2955 level, dealers said.

"If foreign exchange reserves increase as Zhu said, the central bank will continue buying dollars on the market to depress the Chinese currency," one dealer said. "So there will be little change to the yuan's falling trend."

A second dealer said that even though the yuan would be depressed by the central bank, its movement will be stable. UU IJC M Z MF UU FRX CN EMRG #USNSHK006324 FIX CNY4 #MORE R :Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai =3
"The central bank will not let foreign exchange rates fluctuate because it does economic development no particular good," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to test the 8.2960 level again on Wednesday.
The yuan closed up at 6.8205 from 6.8800 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday high of 1.0710 from 1.0707 against the Hong Kong dollar.
